title: GTA 6 Was Never Going to Hit 60 Frames per Second on Consoles
description: IGN Games reports that GTA 6 was never intended to run at 60 fps on consoles, as Rockstar confirms a target of 30 fps across all systems, including the PS5 Pro.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## GTA 6 Was Never Going to Hit 60 Frames per Second on Consoles

As anticipation for Rockstar Games' upcoming masterpiece continues to reach unprecedented heights, the conversation surrounding the game's technical performance on consoles has taken center stage. According to a recent report by gaming media outlet IGN Games, players hoping for a buttery-smooth 60 frames per second on home consoles may need to adjust their expectations, as the game was likely never designed to hit that target in the first place.

### The Writing Was on the Wall

Back when Rockstar first showcased a significant amount of *GTA 6* gameplay footage on Netflix, one technical detail stood out to observant viewers: the game was visibly running at around 30 fps. At the time, segments of the community speculated that this might simply be a byproduct of early-stage builds or promotional video compression. 

However, reality has set in following recent updates. Rockstar has now officially confirmed that it is targeting 30 fps on every console platform, a decision that notably includes even the high-end PS5 Pro. Based on these official confirmations and the initial gameplay showcases, IGN Games points out that it is now abundantly clear the title likely never would have run at a solid 60 fps on console hardware.

### Balancing Scope and Performance

Developing an open-world simulation of this unprecedented scale requires massive computational power. From advanced physics to dense crowds and hyper-detailed environments, Rockstar's ambition for *GTA 6* pushes current console hardware to its absolute limits. Opting for a locked 30 fps target allows developers to maximize graphical fidelity and world simulation density without risking catastrophic performance drops in high-intensity scenarios.

### Editor's Take
While locking at 30 fps on modern consoles—and even the PS5 Pro—might disappoint players accustomed to high framerates, it aligns with Rockstar's historical approach of prioritizing world scale and visual fidelity. If the final product delivers the generational leap in open-world design we all expect, a stable 30 fps will be a compromise most players are willing to accept.
